questions.question: The Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Yojana was started during the _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Eighth Five Year Plan.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Yojana** was started during the** Eighth Five Year Plan**, which was from **1992-1997.**
 
• The aim of the scheme was to provide **employment opportunities** to the** unemployed youth** of the country by promoting **self-employment and entrepreneurship.**
 
• The scheme was later replaced by the **Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) **in **2008**, which continues to provide financial assistance to **start-ups and micro-enterprises.**
 
• The** Seventh Five Year Plan **was from **1985-1990,** **Ninth Five Year Plan** was from **1997-2002**, and **Tenth Five Year Plan **was from **2002-2007**.
 
• Hence, options 1, 3, and 4 are **incorrect.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Yojana **was launched by the** Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises **(MSMEs) and was implemented through the **District Industries Centres (DICs).**
 
• The scheme provided **subsidy up to 15% **of the** project cos**t, subject to a **maximum of Rs. 7,500 per entrepreneur **for setting up of new projects.
 
• The **Seventh Five Year Plan** focused on **accelerating economic growth **and modernizing the industry, while the** Ninth Five Year Plan **emphasized on** poverty reduction **and** human development.**
 
• The **Tenth Five Year Plan** aimed at achieving a **GDP growth rate of 8%** and r**educing poverty** by half.
 
• The **Eighth Five Year Plan**, under which the **Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Yojana **was launched, aimed at increasing **agricultural and industrial production**, improving infrastructure, and promoting social sector development.

questions.question: Which of the following is used to chemically test starch?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** lodine solution.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Iodine solution** is used to **chemically test** for the **presence of starch.**
 
• When iodine solution is added to a sample that contains starch, the solution turns **blue-black** in color.
 
• Chlorine solution is** not **used to test for starch.
 
 
• Chlorine is a **strong oxidizing agent** and can react with **starch**, but this reaction is not specific to starch and can occur with other organic compounds as well.
 
 
 
• Sulphur solution is also** not **used to test for starch.
 
 
• Sulphur is **not known to react** with starch in a way that produces a** visible color change.**
 
 
 
• Bromine solution is **sometimes used to test** for starch, but it is** less **commonly used than iodine solution.
 
 
• When bromine solution is added to a sample that contains starch, the solution turns **orange in color.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Starch** is a** complex carbohydrate** that is commonly found in** plants.**
 
• It is an** important source of energy** for **humans and animals.**
 
• Starch is made up of two types of molecules: **amylose and amylopectin**.
 
• Amylose is a** linear molecule,** while amylopectin is **highly branched.**
 
• Both types of molecules can be detected with **iodine solution.**
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **option 2** (iodine solution) as it specifically reacts with starch to produce a** blue-black color.**

questions.question: Who was the first Odissi dancer from Odisha to receive Padma Vibhushan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Kelucharan Mohapatra. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kelucharan Mohapatra **was a** legendary Odissi dancer, choreographer, and guru,** who played a key role in reviving and popularizing the Odissi dance form in the **20th century.** 
 
• He trained many **notable dancers** and created **numerous compositions **that are still performed today. 
 
• He received the** Padma Vibhushan in 2000**, in recognition of his outstanding contribution to the **field of dance.** 
 
• This was a significant milestone for** Odissi dance** and **Indian classical dance** as a whole, as it helped to elevate their **status and visibility** in the **national and international arena.** 
 
• Mohapatra's style of Odissi was characterized by a **balance of tradition and innovation**, rooted in his deep understanding of the** classical texts, music, and mythology.** 
 
• He also incorporated elements from other **dance forms and cultures, **such as** Kathak and Sufi poetry.** 
 
• Mohapatra's legacy continues to inspire and influence generations of dancers and artists, both in **India and abroad.** 
 
• His contribution to** Odissi dance and Indian culture** has been widely recognized and celebrated, making him a** true icon **of the art form. 
 
• Hence, the **correct **answer is option 3, Kelucharan Mohapatra.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Odissi dance** is **one of the eight classical dance** forms of India, and it originated in the state of **Odisha.**
 
• It is characterized by **fluid body movements**,** intricate footwork**, and **expressive facial expressions.**
 
• **Padma Vibhushan** is the** second-highest civilian award** in India, and it is given for exceptional and distinguished service in any field, including **arts, literature, science, public service, and sports.**
 
• **Sonal Mansingh **(option 1) is also a **renowned Odissi dancer**, as well as a **Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi **dancer.
 
 
• She received the Padma Vibhushan in **2003.**
 
 
 
• **Sanjukta Panigrahi** (option 2) was another prominent** Odissi dancer, **known for her grace and technical virtuosity.
 
 
• She received the Padma Shri in **1975** and the Padma Bhushan in **2004,** but not the Padma Vibhushan.
 
 
 
• **Madhvi Mudgal **(option 4) is a contemporary **Odissi dancer** and choreographer, known for her innovative style and collaborations with other artists.
 
 
• She has been honoured with the Sanskriti Award in 1985, the Padma Shri in 1990, and the Orissa Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1996.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: When did the Drafting Committee publish the first draft of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**February 1948.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Drafting Committee** was a committee appointed by the** Constituent Assembly of India **to draft the Constitution of India. 
 
• The committee was chaired by **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar,** who is considered the **chief architect of the Indian Constitution**. 
 
• The committee had **seven members**, including Ambedkar, and was responsible for drafting the Constitution in a way that would reflect the **aspirations and values **of the Indian people. 
 
• The first draft of the Indian Constitution was published in** February 1948 **by the Drafting Committee chaired by **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.**​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **​Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar, N. Gopalaswami, B.R. Ambedkar, K.M. Munshi, Mohammad Saadulla, B.L. Mitter, and D.P. Khaitan** were among the seven members of the drafting committee.
 
• The inaugural meeting was held on** August 30, 1947.**
 
• On **February 21st, 1948,** the Constitution's** initial draft **was released by the drafting committee.
 
• The inhabitants of India then examined it for around **eight months. **
 
• The Indian Constitution was drafted in its entirety by the drafting committee over the course of** two years, eleven months, and eighteen days **after its founding in 1947.

questions.question: Which of the following states in India, during October to December, receive rainfall due to Northeast monsoon?

options.text: Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Andhra Pradesh
Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Karnataka
Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and West Bengal

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Andhra Pradesh.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Northeast monsoon,** also known as **winter monsoon,** brings rainfall in the** southern part of India** from **October to December.**
 
• **Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Andhra Pradesh **are the states that receive rainfall due to** Northeast monsoon** during this period.
 
• **Punjab, Haryana, and Madhya Pradesh **are located in the **northern part **of India and** do not** receive rainfall due to Northeast monsoon.
 
• **Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka** are located in the** southern part** of India but only Andhra Pradesh receives rainfall due to Northeast monsoon.
 
 
• Karnataka receives rainfall during **Southwest monsoon** from **June to September.**
 
 
 
• **Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and West Bengal** are located in the **northern and eastern parts **of India and **do not** receive rainfall due to Northeast monsoon.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Northeast monsoon **is caused by the** reversal of wind direction** over the Indian Ocean, which brings **moisture from the Bay of Bengal **to the southern part of India.
 
• **Tamil Nadu** is the state that receives the **highest amount of rainfall** due to** Northeast monsoon,** followed by **Kerala and Andhra Pradesh.**
 
• **Punjab, Haryana, and Madhya Pradesh** are located in the** arid and semi-arid regions **of India and receive most of their rainfall during **Southwest monsoon.**
 
• **Andhra Pradesh** receives rainfall both during S**outhwest monsoon and Northeast monsoon** due to its location on the east coast of India.

questions.question: Which of the following has the highest value of resistivity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nichrome.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Resistivity** is the **measure **of how strongly a material opposes the** flow of electric current** through it.
 
• **Nichrome **has the **highest value of resistivity** among the given options because it is an **alloy **made of** nickel, chromium, and iron**, which are all metals with **high resistivity.**
 
• **Silver **has the **lowest value of resistivity **among the given options because it is a **good conductor of electricity **due to its low resistivity.
 
• **Chromium** has a **higher value of resistivity than iron** because it is a more **brittle metal** and has a **higher melting point.**
 
• **Iron** has a **lower value of resistivity **than nichrome because it is a **good conductor of electricity** and has a** lower resistance** to the flow of electric current.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Silver** is a good conductor of electricity and is often used in **electronics and electrical wiring** due to its low resistivity.
 
• **Nichrome** is commonly used in** heating elements**, as it has a high resistivity and can withstand **high temperatures.**
 
• **Chromium** is used in the production of **stainless steel,** as it has a high resistance to** corrosion and oxidation.**
 
• **Iron** is used in **construction, machinery, and transportation **due to its strength and durability.

questions.question: On 20 July 2021, the Supreme Court struck down certain provisions of part IX B of the Constitution of India. Part IX B was related to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Co-operative Societies.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **The correct answer is option 3, i.e., Co-operative Societies. Part IX B of the Constitution of India deals with the provisions related to the formation and functioning of cooperative societies.**
 
• The Supreme Court has struck down specific provisions of** Part IX B, which means that some rules related to cooperative societies are no longer valid.**
 
• Co-operative societies are formed by a group of individuals who come together to pool their resources and work towards a common goal.
 
• These societies can be formed for various purposes, such as agricultural, industrial, housing, etc.
 
• Cooperative societies play an essential role in the country's socioeconomic development as they provide a platform for the members to work together and achieve their common objectives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Panchayats **- Part IX of the Constitution deals with the provisions related to Panchayats. Panchayats are the local village, intermediate, and district self-government bodies.
 
• **Municipalities **- Part IXA of the Constitution deals with the provisions related to Municipalities. Municipalities are the local self-government bodies at the urban level.
 
• **Sub-ordinate Courts -** Part VI of the Constitution deals with the provisions related to the Union Judiciary. Subordinate courts are the lower courts that operate under the supervision of the higher courts. -

questions.question: which of the following Indian states was the host of the 36th national games?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Gujarat.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• The **36th National Games **of India were held in **Gujarat.**
 
• The games took place across **six cities** in the state: **Ahmedabad, Gandhinagar, Surat, Vadodara, Rajkot, and Bhavnagar.**
 
• Almost** 7,000 athletes** from 28 Indian states, eight Union Territories, and Services, the sports team of the Indian Armed Forces, competed for medals in 36 different sports.

questions.question: Which element of Group 17 has two isotopes of masses 35 and 37 amu with average abundance of 75.77% and 24.23%, respectively?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chlorine.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Chlorine is the element of **Group 17 **that has two isotopes of** masses 35 and 37 amu.**
 
• The average abundance of the **isotopes is 75.77%** for **35 amu** and **24.23% for 37 amu.**
 
• Chlorine has the **atomic number 17** and its chemical symbol is **Cl.**
 
• Chlorine is a pungent,** green-yellow gas at room temperature** and makes up about** 0.0018% **of the Earth's crust.
 
• It's widely known for its use in **disinfecting drinking water** as well as in** bleach and other cleaning products**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iodine:**

 
 
• Iodine is another member of **Group 17,** the **Halogens**. It has one stable isotope:** Iodine-127.**
 
• It is a shiny**, dark-grey to purple-black** nonmetal that can be seen when it is at room temperature.
 
• Iodine is essential for the production of thyroid hormones in the human body, with **deficiency leading to goitre**, an enlargement of the thyroid gland.
 
• Its** radioisotope, iodine-131**, is used in **medical treatment, particularly for thyroid conditions.**
 
 
 
• **Fluorine:**
 
 
• Fluorine is the lightest member of the** halogens** and has only one stable isotope: **Fluorine-19.**
 
• It is a **pale, yellow-green gas** at room temperature and is the** most reactive and electronegative** of all elements.
 
• The majority of fluorine is used in the manufacture of a variety of compounds, including an important class called** fluorocarbons**, that have many **industrial applications.**
 
 
 
• **Astatine:**
 
 
• Astatine is a halogen and the** heaviest **element in **Group 17.** It is a radioactive element, and all its isotopes are short-lived; the **most stable isotope, Astatine-210, has a half-life of 8.1 hours.**
 
• It is the** rarest naturally occurring element** and is typically **produced synthetically.**
 
• Not much is known about astatine due to its scarcity, but it's believed to be a heavy, volatile, and highly reactive metalloid similar to the other halogens.

questions.question: Which of the following countries never hosted the Paralympic games ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** India.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **India has never hosted the Paralympic games.**
 
• The Paralympic Games are an international multi-sport event **for athletes with disabilities.**
 
• It is held** every four years**, following the Olympic games. 
 
• The** first Paralympic games **were held in** Rome, Italy in 1960.**
 
• Since then, it has grown to become the world's** third-largest sporting event**, after the Olympic games and the FIFA World Cup.
 
• The Paralympic games feature a wide range of sports, including **athletics, swimming, wheelchair basketball, and sitting volleyball, among others.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Israel** hosted the Paralympic Games in **Tel Aviv in 1968,** which is the only time the games have been held in the Middle East.
 
• **Japan** hosted the Paralympic Games in **1964 in Tokyo**, and again in the **Summer Paralympics 2020 (held in 2021 due to the COVID-19 pandemic).**
 
• **South Korea** hosted the Paralympic Games in** Seoul in 1988 **and again in the **Winter Paralympics 2018 in PyeongChang.**

questions.question: The ‘Right to Work’ plan, under the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005, was Implemented in how many districts in the first phase?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** 200.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The 'Right to Work' **plan was implemented in** 200 districts in the first phase **under the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, of 2005.
 
• This plan aims to provide **at least 100 days of wage employment** to every household in rural areas. 
 
• The plan ensures that workers receive timely payment for** their work and prohibits discrimination based on gender, caste, or religion.**
 
• The plan also provides for the creation of durable assets such as **water conservation structures, rural roads, and irrigation canals.**
 
• The act was later renamed as the **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) in 2009. **
 
• MGNREGA is a "rights-based" programme, where the workers who are willing to do manual, unskilled labour are guaranteed work at a minimum wage.
 
• **If work is not provided **to the worker within 15 days of applying, then the **state government is liable to pay an unemployment allowance.**
